events.label: FOMC meeting Day 1 — no decision; final pre-announcement positioning with Brent $90, September hike ~78%
events.note: Updated as of July 27 night: FOMC meets July 28-29 with Chair Kevin Warsh presiding (decision 2pm ET July 29, press conference 2:30pm ET). Context entering Day 1: (1) US-Iran mutual pause held intact through Monday session — Brent at $90.28 (above $85 trigger, but well below the $100.69 Saturday high); (2) NVDA -5% on circular AI financing report (WSJ/Bloomberg: NVDA in talks to backstop $250B OpenAI data center financing, $350B chip financing separately — total $500B+ project) — AI demand organic-vs-manufactured question now at WSJ-level public market event; (3) CXMT $487B Shanghai IPO (+466% first day) = Chinese memory competition accelerating; (4) Durable Goods +0.3% vs +2.5% expected — dovish manufacturing signal. September hike probability ~78% (directionally repriced from 82% on Brent retreat + Durable Goods miss, still above 70% trigger). Day 1 no formal signal expected; watch 10Y: above 4.68% signals bond market expects hawkish hold with September live; below 4.60% signals dovish surprise pricing.

events.label: FOMC Decision (2pm ET) + Warsh press conf (2:30pm) + META Q2 AH + MSFT Q4 FY26 AH — year's most event-dense session
events.note: Updated as of July 27 night: FOMC rate decision 2pm ET, Warsh press conference 2:30pm ET, then META Q2 AH (EPS est $7.23, Rev est $60.3B; 87% prediction-market beat prob) and MSFT Q4 FY26 AH (EPS est $4.24, Rev est $87.6B; Azure 40%+ growth must justify FY27 CapEx est $262B) — all in the same session. NEW CONTEXT added July 27: (1) NVDA circular financing report reframes MSFT's capex scrutiny — MSFT is a named AI infrastructure partner; if FOMC signals hawkish hold AND MSFT guides $262B capex without credible AI monetization ROI, the circular financing concern extends to MSFT's own capex loop; (2) CXMT $487B IPO signals Chinese competition accelerating in memory — AMZN and MSFT Azure host Chinese AI models (Kimi K3 on AWS/Modal) which may cannibalize inference demand from closed-weight API providers; (3) Durable Goods miss = dovish signal entering FOMC, but tariffs + Brent $90 keep hawkish case defensible. Dovish Warsh (September below 55%): TLT rally, upgrade clock potentially starts Day 1 if SPX closes above 7,480. Hawkish Warsh (September live): 30Y breaks 5.20%, SPX tests 7,380 BEARISH level. META AI ad ROI vs. $40B+ AI spend is the META swing variable. MSFT Azure growth vs. $262B FY27 capex commitment — now also read through the circular financing lens — is the MSFT binary.

events.label: AAPL Q2 AH + AMZN Q2 AH + Q2 GDP Advance Estimate (8:30 AM ET) — final Mag-7 and first GDP read
events.note: Updated as of July 27 night: Three catalysts in one session. Q2 GDP advance estimate at 8:30am ET (est. +2-3% annualized vs. Q1 positive) — a below-2% print would open stagflation discussion independent of FOMC language; above 3% eases hard-landing concern. AAPL Q2 AH: AAPL overtook NVDA as largest US company by market cap on July 27 ($336.50, +1.1%) — the rotation signal is confirmed. China iPhone units and services gross margin vs. App Store pressure are the key metrics. EPS est $1.89, Rev est $108.9B. Oil retreat + DXY pullback constructive for China-heavy revenue base. AMZN Q2 AH: AWS is the near-term beneficiary of Kimi K3 day-0 hosted inference demand (Together AI and Modal) before on-prem self-hosting ramps — can AMZN argue AI inference volume is AWS-additive in its call? EPS est $1.82, Rev est $196.7B; AWS est +32% growth. If AAPL China beats AND AMZN AWS confirms +30%+ AI demand growth AND Q2 GDP above 2%: upgrade clock could approach Day 2 by Friday July 31.

events.note: Palantir reports Q2 2026 AH on August 3. Options market is pricing approximately a 15% earnings swing (noted July 27). events.label: July CPI (est.) — Brent oil shock + Trump tariffs on 99.4% of imports; dual inflation embedding, partially moderated by Iran pause
events.note: Updated as of July 27 night: Two major inflation inputs, with the first partially moderated by the Iran mutual pause. (1) Brent crude: averaged ~$97-100 for multiple sessions before the July 27 US-Iran pause sent Brent to $90. Gasoline follows Brent with a 2-3 week lag — the $97-100 period (roughly July 14-24) is already embedded in the gasoline component of August CPI; the post-pause retreat ($89-90) will partially offset but cannot fully reverse the embedded pass-through. Net CPI oil contribution: materially positive but not the worst-case $100+ ceiling scenario. (2) Trump's 10-12.5% tariffs on 99.4% of US imports (effective July 24) remain the second inflationary input, adding import cost pressure across consumer goods, autos, and industrial inputs. September cumulative hike probability ~78% per July 27 close estimate. A July CPI print above 3.5% YoY still makes September near-certain. Bull scenario (CPI ≤3.0%): oil pass-through didn't fully embed in core by August 13; September probability falls below 50%. Bear scenario (CPI ≥3.8%): dual oil+tariff pass-through exceeds expectations; September 50bps probability above 90%, BEARISH regime re-activated.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — must address AMD hyperscaler sweep + Kimi K3 + CXMT + circular financing disclosure
events.note: Updated as of July 27 night: NVDA Q2 FY27 is the fundamental clearing event for the AI GPU thesis. $91B revenue guidance represents sequential acceleration. Context updated July 27: (1) AMD keynote confirmed all four major hyperscalers as Helios customers — most credible competitive diversification from Nvidia in AI cycle history; (2) Kimi K3 full open weights released July 27 (Sunday night) — 2.8T parameters, 70% inference pricing discount thesis now in the market; (3) CXMT $487B Shanghai IPO July 27 — Chinese memory competition entering at government-backed scale; (4) NEW: WSJ/Bloomberg circular financing report July 27 — NVDA in talks to backstop $250B in OpenAI data center financing; on the Q2 FY27 call, analysts will press on whether Q2 revenue includes any demand that is directly or indirectly financed by NVDA itself; (5) TSMC wafer hike margins unresolved. Hard stop $216 intact; do not add until Q2 FY27 addresses all five factors with data.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off -13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst. Note: the NVDA circular financing story (July 27) — NVDA in talks to backstop $250B in OpenAI data center financing — adds complexity to the OpenAI IPO timeline if the guarantee structure is disclosed in S-1 filings.
